REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - OCTOBER 25, 2018 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
OCTOBER 25, 2018, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Pastor Robin Kim, Artesia-Cerritos United Methodist
  Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Recreation Services Division Youth
  Flag Football Pee Wee Team – Giants and Coach Adrian Lomeli.

4.  Roll Call

  attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Mark E. Pulido

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Scout Award).

  Rhonda Burd and Darshna Shah, Volunteer Coordinators (Cerritos/Artesia
  Distinguished Young Women Program).

  Audrey Hsu (2019 California State Distinguished Young Woman).

  Ananya Narayanan (2nd Alternate 2019 California State Distinguished Young
  Woman).

  Vacation Connection (Business Spotlight).

5B.  Consideration of appointments to Commissions and Committees.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Hu, to appoint Karen
  Wilson to fill an unexpired term on the Community Safety Committee ending
  March 31, 2019.

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None

  ABSTAIN:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration of a written appeal of a decision of the Property
  Preservation Commission denying a request to remove a parkway tree adjacent
  to the property located at 12544 Rose Street, Cerritos, California (APN 7025-
  017-005), Property Preservation Commission Case No. TR 2018-9 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Todd Kuh, Parks Superintendent. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Carol Smith expressed concern as to the parkway tree roots adjacent to the
  subject property and requested pruning of the roots if the tree removal were to
  be denied.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  the public hearing and public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to direct staff to
  prune the roots of the subject tree on the side of the property at 12544 Rose
  Street, Cerritos, California (APN 7025-017-005), as necessary (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8B.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and adopt A RESOLUTION OF

  FAMILY TRUST, TO PERMIT A COMMERCIAL RECREATION FACILITY USE, SKY
  ZONE INDOOR TRAMPOLINE PARK, IN AN EXISTING SHOPPING CENTER
  LOCATED AT 10755 SOUTH STREET, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA, 90703. THE
  SUBJECT PROPERTY IS ZONED NEIGHBORHOOD COMMERCIAL (CN) (APN
  7038-007-007) (COUNCIL).*

  *Pursuant to Section 15301 of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA),
  this project is categorically exempt from CEQA review.

  A staff report was given by Sandy Cisneros, Senior Planner. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Irfan Ahmed, owner of SkyZone Trampoline Park, expressed support for the subject
  project.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  (continued next page)

8C.  Review and consideration of a request by First Transit Incorporated, for a
  proposed contract amendment for the Cerritos on Wheels (COW) and Dial-a-Ride
  transportation services in response to new California minimum wage laws and
  subcontractor wage restructuring (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Dax Sikes, Director of Operations Southwest, First Transit Incorporated, expressed
  support for the proposal.

  Gerard Lindsmiier, Vice President of Business Development, Secure Transportation,
  spoke in support of the program. He read a letter of support written by Cerritos
  resident, Brian Tom.

  Chris Calderon, Dispatch Manager of Secure Transportation, spoke in support of the
  program.

  Noting there were no further individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Hu, to authorize the City
  Manager to take all necessary steps to facilitate the modification of the existing
  First Transit/City contract to include modified contract rates for the Cerritos on
  Wheels and Dial-A-Ride transportation services, resulting in an annual increase
  of $40,000 per year beginning with the 2018-2019 Fiscal Year through the
  2022-2023 Fiscal Year Budget, with no modification to existing Saturday
  Cerritos on Wheels service (COUNCIL).
  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:
  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

8D.  Review and consideration of a request for authorization for the City of Cerritos
  (Seller) to sell City-owned property located at 17423 Studebaker Road, Cerritos,
  California, 90703, to AutoNation (Buyer), pursuant to terms of a Letter of Intent
  (LOI). The subject property is zoned Development Area Fifteen (ADP-15), with
  an overlay zoning designation of Area Development Plan 5.1 (ADP-5.1) Cerritos
  Auto Square Overlay Zone, measures approximately ‡1.19 acres, and is
  currently vacant and undeveloped (APN 7034-016-910) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kristin Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  Paul W. Bellenbaum spoke regarding utilizing the subject property for electric
  vehicles.

  Noting there were further no individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed
  public comments.

  MOTION DID NOT PASS: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Hu, to
  authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to continue negotiations with
  AutoNation to develop and prepare a formal Purchase and Sale Agreement,
  consistent with the terms contained within the Letter of Intent, subject to
  review and approval by the Cerritos City Council at an upcoming publically-
  noticed City Council meeting (COUNCIL).
  The motion did not pass (2 – 3) as follows:
  AYES:  Edwards, Hu
  NOES:  Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  There was no further action taken on this item.

9.  New and Old Business
9A.  Review and consideration of playground equipment at Reservoir Hill Park
  (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Sherré Titus, Recreation Services Superintendent. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Edwards, and seconded by Solanki, to select the
  Shine color palette for the proposed playground equipment for Reservoir Hill Park
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Yokoyama, Solanki, Pulido
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
